work_order.root_cause: The report's category selection reaches the amounts but never reaches the row axis, and it misses the axis in two distinct places because categoryLists returns two independently-derived halves from one call and the table reads only the second. The selection arrives solely as a `category oneOf [...]` query filter applied inside makeQuery, so an unselected category correctly contributes 0 to every amount. Meanwhile custom-spreadsheet.ts:87 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:39 both call categoryLists(categories) on the raw unfiltered `categories` from useCategories(). categoryLists returns `categoryList`, built from `categories.list` (ReportOptions.ts:387-401), and `categoryGroup`, built as a verbatim copy `[...categories.grouped, uncategorizedGroup]` (ReportOptions.ts:403-406). Everything the Split=Category table view actually renders comes from that second half: grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94 maps `categoryGroup` for the group rows and lines 110-111 map each group's nested `categories`, which are the embedded arrays populated server-side by getCategories and are never derived from `categories.list`. So a fix that narrows only `list` cannot reach the table view at all, and groupBySelections' 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' cases both build their axis from `categoryGroup`, so they miss it too. This is why the first plan's grouped-spreadsheet.ts edit was inert. filterEmptyRows is the only thing that ever reconciled the two sides, and it does so destructively: with showEmpty false it drops every zero row, which incidentally drops the unselected categories and hides the defect; with showEmpty true it returns true unconditionally (filterEmptyRows.ts:24), so all the unselected rows survive at 0.00. 'Show empty rows' is not overriding the selection - it is removing the only filter that was hiding the fact that the selection never reached the axis. The same asymmetry already has a correct implementation elsewhere: fetchBudgetData calls filterCategoriesByConditions to narrow its data (budgetDataQuery.ts:203-208), which is why Budgeted's amounts were already correct - but its axis, built from the same un-narrowed categoryLists, was not, as the reproduction above shows.
work_order.approach: Narrow BOTH halves of the category axis at the point the two spreadsheets build it, reusing the existing filterCategoriesByConditions helper in budgetDataQuery.ts rather than inventing a second predicate. Add one exported helper, narrowCategoriesByConditions(categories, conditions, conditionsOp), that calls filterCategoriesByConditions to get the surviving `list`, then derives the surviving id set and maps `categories.grouped` to a new array whose each group's `categories` is intersected with that set, dropping groups left with an empty `categories` array. Both factories call this once and pass the narrowed `{list, grouped}` to categoryLists. Narrowing `grouped` - not `list` alone - is what makes the table view correct: grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94-111 and the 'Group'/'CategoryGroup' branches of groupBySelections read only the grouped half. Three deliberate details, each verified in this run rather than argued. First, the helper returns `categories` unchanged (by identity) when filterCategoriesByConditions returns its input unchanged, which is what it does for an absent, empty, non-category, or unsafely-interpretable condition set; that preserves the conservative 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' fallback and means a group that is legitimately empty in an unfiltered report is not silently dropped. I confirmed all three of those fallbacks behave correctly (empty group survives with conditions [], a 'hasTags' condition narrows nothing, both by identity). Second, the synthetic `uncategorizedGroup` is appended by categoryLists itself after whatever `grouped` it is given (ReportOptions.ts:403-406), so it is out of reach of this narrowing by construction and the Uncategorized/Off budget block survives - it is out_of_scope here and must not be filtered away. Confirmed in the browser: post-fix, Uncategorized/Transfers/Off budget still render. Third, Type=Budgeted is deliberately NOT excluded. custom-spreadsheet.ts builds its axis with categoryLists for every balanceTypeOp including 'totalBudgeted', and the reproduction shows Budgeted has the same phantom rows today, so the narrowing applies there too and the phantom zero rows disappear there too. That is the same defect corrected on a second surface, not a regression - see AC-7, which is written to say so and is verified by a test that can actually fail. Keep passing the unfiltered `categories.list`/`categories.grouped` to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData in both factories, so the query-side filter is untouched and both sides are computed from the same expression. Keep filterEmptyRows unchanged; it is correct for its job and is only ever exposed by this bug. Do not special-case groupBy - the defect is upstream of the split, in the shared axis.

files.change: Add and export `narrowCategoriesByConditions(categories, conditions, conditionsOp)` immediately above the existing `filterCategoriesByConditions` (which begins at line 75). It takes `{ list: CategoryEntity[]; grouped: CategoryGroupEntity[] }` and returns the same shape, narrowed by conditions. Implementation, verified end-to-end in this run: call `filterCategoriesByConditions(categories.list, categories.grouped, conditions, conditionsOp)` to get `list`; if the returned array is `categories.list` by identity - the helper's signal that no condition narrowed anything - return `categories` unchanged and stop. Otherwise build `const keep = new Set(list.map(c => c.id))`, map `categories.grouped` to `categories.grouped.map(g => ({ ...g, categories: (g.categories ?? []).filter(c => keep.has(c.id)) }))`, then `.filter(g => g.categories.length > 0)` to drop groups emptied by the narrowing, and return `{ list, grouped }`. The identity check is load-bearing, not an optimisation: without it, a genuinely empty category group would be dropped from every unfiltered report in the product. Keep the existing `filterCategoriesByConditions` byte-identical - it is used by fetchBudgetData and is covered by budgetDataQuery.test.ts, and the fix is additive.
files.why: Both spreadsheet factories need the identical narrowing, and putting it beside the existing helper keeps one definition of 'which categories does this condition select' in the codebase instead of two that can drift.

Post-fix, 'Show empty rows' ON with Bills-only selected rendered 'Bills -3,050.00 / Cell -150.00 / Internet -120.00 / Mortgage -2,400.00 / Water -180.00 / Power -200.00 / Uncategorized & Off budget 0.00 / Uncategorized 0.00 / Transfers 0.00 / Off budget 0.00' - the 23 phantom rows are gone and the synthetic block correctly survives. Console/network during the reproductions: no application errors and no failed requests attributable to this bug. Code corroboration, read after the reproduction: CustomReport.tsx:267 computes `selectedCategories` from the filter conditions and passes it only to ReportSidebar for rendering the checkboxes, while createGroupedSpreadsheet (line 515) and createCustomSpreadsheet (line 551) both receive the raw unfiltered `categories` from useCategories() (line 152). categoryLists (ReportOptions.ts:381-408) derives its two axis halves from different inputs: categoryList from `categories.list` (lines 387-401) and categoryGroup as a verbatim `[...categories.grouped, uncategorizedGroup]` (lines 403-406). grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94 maps categoryGroup for group rows and lines 110-111 map each group's nested `categories`. ReportTableList.tsx:28-31 selects data.groupedData when groupBy === 'Category', and ReportTable.tsx:159 renders id="list". groupBySelections (ReportOptions.ts:412-473): 'Category' and 'Interval' read categoryList; 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' both read categoryGroup; 'Payee' and 'Account' read payees/accounts. The selection reaches the amounts only as a query filter inside makeQuery via fetchSpreadsheetQueryData, so unselected categories correctly contribute 0. filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:24, `return !showEmpty ? showHide : true`) is the only thing that ever hid this. fetchSpreadsheetQueryData.ts:40-51 routes totalBudgeted to fetchBudgetData, which calls filterCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:203-208) - that is why Budgeted's amounts were already right while its axis was not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Narrow only `categories.list` (what the first plan specified) and leave `grouped` untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Structurally inert for the reported symptom, and this is the objection the plan review raised against v1. categoryLists builds categoryGroup as a verbatim copy of `categories.grouped`, and each group's nested `categories` are the embedded arrays populated server-side by getCategories - neither is derived from `list`. Everything the Split=Category table view renders comes from that second half (grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94, 110-111), as do the 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' branches of groupBySelections. Confirmed empirically in this run: on unmodified code the closure-driven axis prints c-food and c-rent in both the Category axis and the Group axis, and groupedData contains g-usual with nested [c-food, c-rent]. Narrowing `list` alone would have fixed the graphs and left the reporter's table and both group rows fully intact.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it inside filterEmptyRows - make showEmpty-aware filtering also drop rows belonging to unselected categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That treats the symptom. filterEmptyRows only sees a GroupedEntity and its flag; it has no knowledge of the selection conditions, so honouring the selection there would mean threading the whole condition set through a function whose job is a zero/nonzero test. It would also leave the axis itself wrong - every unselected category would still be computed, summed into totals and handed to the legend and the graph on every render, and any other consumer of the axis would keep seeing the phantom rows. The debugger rule is to fix what produces the bad value, and the bad value is the row axis.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it in CustomReport.tsx by passing selectedCategories into the spreadsheet factories instead of the full categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tempting and much smaller, but wrong in two ways. First, useSelectedCategories (CustomReport.tsx:73-113) only understands a 'category' field with is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf and deliberately returns the FULL list for every other condition shape - including category_group conditions, text operators, and the multiple-category-condition case that isComplexCategoryCondition exists to flag. So this would narrow the axis for simple selections and silently do nothing for the complex ones, an inconsistency users would hit and could not explain. Second, categories.grouped is still needed for the Group split and for per-group rows, so the prop would have to be split in two anyway - which is the same shape as the helper being added, but in the wrong layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Filter inside categoryLists() in ReportOptions.ts, since both factories call it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: categoryLists takes only { list, grouped } and no conditions, so filtering there would require changing its signature to accept the conditions - turning a pure shape helper into one that silently drops rows based on a second input. Its existing sibling callers and its single-responsibility shape (build the three axis lists plus the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget/Transfers rows) would be lost. Narrowing at the two factories that own the spreadsheet inputs, via one shared helper, keeps categoryLists pure.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the row filter as a new, narrower predicate local to custom-spreadsheet.ts, handling only the category oneOf/is/isNot/notOneOf shape.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Duplicates filterCategoriesByConditions, which already implements exactly this and is already covered by budgetDataQuery.test.ts (category, category_group, oneOf, text operators, combined and/or). A second predicate would drift from it and would have no equivalent of its 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' guard, which is the safety property that keeps complex-condition reports from silently losing rows.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop groups whose categories are all filtered out, without the identity guard on an unnarrowed condition set.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This silently deletes any group that is legitimately empty in an unfiltered report - a user with an empty group would see it disappear from every custom report in the product, a behaviour change unrelated to this bug. Guarding on `list === categories.list` (exactly what filterCategoriesByConditions returns when it declines to narrow) makes the rebuild happen only when something was actually narrowed. Verified in this session: with the guard, conditions [] preserves a group with categories: []; under a real narrowing it is dropped, as intended.

alternatives_considered.approach: Exclude balanceTypeOp 'totalBudgeted' from the narrowing, so the Budgeted axis is left exactly as it is today.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected on the evidence, and this is the second plan-review objection read back into the approach. Budgeted does not have a working axis today: I reproduced the identical phantom block on the Budgeted axis in the pre-fix browser (Step 7). Excluding it would mean knowingly shipping a fix for 'unchecked categories render at 0.00 despite being deselected' while special-casing one Type value to keep exhibiting it. The narrow risk of applying it to Budgeted is that the axis changes - and that change is the same correction, losing only rows that are 0.00 by construction. Budgeted's amounts were already correct and are untouched, because fetchSpreadsheetQueryData keeps receiving the unfiltered categories and still calls filterCategoriesByConditions itself. AC-7 is written to check exactly that, and to fail if the amounts move.

risks: Over-narrowing is the real hazard. filterCategoriesByConditions returns its input unchanged when it cannot safely interpret a condition, and that fallback is load-bearing: it is what keeps reports using complex category conditions (the isComplexCategoryCondition set in CustomReport.tsx - multiple category conditions, category_group conditions, contains/doesNotContain/matches/hasTags/hasAnyTag) rendering every row they render today. The identity guard in files[0] is what carries this property through the new helper and it is easy to drop in implementation. AC-4 and AC-10 exist to catch exactly that, and I verified both fallbacks behave correctly before writing them down.

Dropping emptied groups is a second way to over-narrow, and it is new behaviour filterCategoriesByConditions has no analogue for: a group whose categories are all filtered out disappears entirely rather than rendering at 0.00. That is the intended reading of the reporter's request - 'even show empty rows in that group' only makes sense if groups outside it are hidden, and it matches the sidebar's 'Hide unchecked' control - but it is a judgement call, and it is why the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget block must be left alone. That block is appended by categoryLists after the narrowing and so is safe by construction, but an implementer who 'helpfully' also filtered it would remove a block the reporter never complained about. AC-9 and the e2e case 'The synthetic block still renders' both guard it.

Two factories change and the second is load-bearing for the reported symptom. In Split=Category the table renders data.groupedData (ReportTableList.tsx:28-31), which comes from createGroupedSpreadsheet. An implementer who edits only custom-spreadsheet.ts will see the graphs corrected and the table still wrong, and may conclude the fix failed. I observed exactly this split behaviour: the grouped half is what the table reads, so files[2] is not a sibling cleanup.

Two callers exist and both are affected. GetCardData.tsx (lines 127 and 146) calls the same two factories for dashboard report widgets, passing its own `categories` prop and the saved report's conditions. Because the fix lives inside the factories, dashboard widgets are corrected by the same change and need no edit - but this change alters dashboard widget output, which is outside what the reporter described. It is the correct behaviour (a widget showing a filtered report should not render unselected rows) and the shared-function argument is what makes it right, but it should be a conscious acceptance rather than a surprise at review. I did not exercise this path in a browser within this run.

Type=Budgeted's rendered output changes by this fix, deliberately. The pre-fix browser run shows its axis carrying the same phantom zero rows as the Payment path, so narrowing removes them. The amounts must not move, and AC-7 checks that with a real (unstubbed-at-the-top) Budgeted run rather than by argument - a named failure mode of the previous version of this criterion was that its named tests could not detect the change either way.
out_of_scope: The synthetic Uncategorized / Off budget / Transfers rows that categoryLists always appends. They appeared at 0.00 in the reproduction, but they are appended unconditionally by design (ReportOptions.ts:398-400, 403-406) and are governed by the showUncategorized and showOffBudget flags, not by the category selection. They survive the narrowing by construction; AC-9 asserts they are still present so that an implementer does not extend the narrowing to them. AC-1 and AC-2 are worded to exclude this block explicitly for the same reason - it is the one thing that would otherwise make those two criteria false against AC-9.

Payee and Account splits. They are not affected by this defect - groupBySelections builds those axes from `payees`/`accounts` (ReportOptions.ts:453-465), which carry no category selection - so no change to them is needed and none is claimed.

The two React 'Encountered two children with the same key' console warnings. They reproduce on the untouched page before any interaction, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this bug - filing them here would bury this fix.

Renaming the user-facing string 'Show empty rows'. The reporter called it 'show unused rows', but the label in the running app is 'Show empty rows' and matches its tooltip ('Show rows that are zero or blank'). The label is accurate; only the interaction with selection is wrong.

The QA and e2e steps above uncheck the checkboxes individually to reach the same state. Adding the control would be a separate, user-facing feature and is not needed to fix this bug.
assumptions: Dropping a group whose categories are all filtered out, rather than rendering it at 0.00, is the intended reading of the reporter's request. The reporter asks to 'even show empty rows in that group', which is only consistent with hiding groups outside it, and it matches the sidebar's 'Hide unchecked' control. The ticket does not state a boundary for the synthetic block, which is why that is left alone rather than decided here.

filterCategoriesByConditions is the intended narrowing helper. Its semantics match what is needed - it understands both condition fields and carries the conservative fallback - and its existing use on the Budgeted path shows the codebase already treats it as the canonical answer to this question. If a maintainer prefers a different helper, the diagnosis and the reproduction still hold; only the approach would change.

Passing the unfiltered categories to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData while narrowing only the axis is correct, because the query needs the full list to evaluate the condition itself. This follows from makeQuery applying the conditions as a filter, and from fetchBudgetData narrowing its own data internally.

The narrowed {list, grouped} pair is safe to hand to categoryLists even though its two halves are no longer verbatim derivable from each other. categoryLists only uses `grouped` to look up sort_order/is_income for sorting `list` (lines 387-393), and the narrowing keeps the two consistent, so the sort is undisturbed.

Type=Budgeted should be corrected by this fix rather than exempted from it. This is a judgement call made on reproduced evidence rather than on the ticket, and it is the one place where a maintainer might reasonably want a narrower scope; the objection to exempting it is recorded in alternatives_considered so it can be overruled deliberately rather than by omission.
unknowns: Whether unchecking a category has always produced this, or whether it is a regression. review.title: Under conditionsOp 'or' with a non-category condition, narrowing the axis by the category condition alone silently drops fetched transactions from the report AND from its totals. The query side ORs every condition; the axis side ORs only the category ones.
review.detail:
Under conditionsOp 'or' with a non-category condition, narrowing the axis by the category condition alone silently drops fetched transactions from the report AND from its totals. The query side ORs every condition; the axis side ORs only the category ones.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:86`

Evidence: Two conditions reachable together in the UI: the sidebar produces `{field:'category', op:'oneOf', value:[A]}` (CustomReport.tsx:232 setSelectedCategories) and the topbar FilterButton adds e.g. `{field:'payee', op:'is', value:'X'}` (ReportTopbar.tsx:234). ConditionsOpMenu.tsx renders the all/any FieldSelect whenever `conditions.length > 1`, so conditionsOp='or' is user-selectable. With conditionsOp='or': (1) custom-spreadsheet.ts:120 sets conditionsOpKey='$or' and makeQuery.ts:20 filters `{ $or: filters }` over the AQL built from BOTH conditions by `make-filters-from-conditions`, so a transaction in unselected category B paid to payee X IS fetched; (2) narrowCategoriesByConditions -> filterCategoriesByConditions builds `categoryConditions` from `conditions.filter(cond => !cond.customName && (field==='category'||field==='category_group'))` (budgetDataQuery.ts:86-98) - the payee condition is not in that list - then applies `op === 'or' ? categoryConditions.some(...) : every(...)` (budgetDataQuery.ts:173-177), so B fails the single category condition and is dropped from both `list` and `grouped`; (3) totalAssets/totalDebts/netAssets/totalTotals in custom-spreadsheet.ts:180-250 are accumulated by iterating `groupByList`, which no longer contains B, so B's fetched amounts are excluded from the totals too. Pre-fix B was on the axis and its amounts were counted, so the fix changes a report total. No test exercises conditionsOp='or' - all seven cases in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts use baseProps' 'and'.

Fix: Only narrow the axis when the category conditions are the whole story: bail out to the identity return when conditionsOp === 'or' and `conditions.length !== categoryConditions.length` (i.e. a non-category condition participates in the OR). Add a unit case with conditionsOp='or' and a second, non-category condition asserting the axis is left unfiltered.

review.title: The JSDoc on `narrowCategoriesByConditions` asserts an invariant the function does not hold: that it narrows 'using the same conditions the query side is filtered by'.
